item.title: China accuses US of 'fabricating' Nvidia spy claims to push tech 'blockade'
item.description: China on Thursday accused the United States of “fabricating spy narratives” to justify a technology “blockade”, stepping up its pushback against reports that the woman Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with was a Chinese intelligence asset.

item.title: Bomb alert at Calais train station affects Eurostar
item.description: A bomb alert is under way at a French train station, with Eurostar trains affected.

item.title: Pope Leo returns to beloved former home of Chiclayo, Peru
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is celebrated in Chiclayo, Peru, where his image is ubiquitous

item.title: Democrat Colom flips Mississippi Senate seat
item.description: Democrat Scott Colom will win the election for U.S. Senate in Mississippi, The Associated Press projects.

item.title: Burnham says climate crisis is 'upon all of us now' and commits UK to 2050 net-zero target
item.description: The prime minister has declared the "climate crisis is upon all of us now" and committed the UK to meeting its 2050 net zero target.

item.title: Iran live updates: Tehran says it will hit US bases if Pickaxe Mountain attacked
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: Who is Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang?
item.description: Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to decide whether to oust CEO ​Jensen Huang, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters, as the world's dominant supplier of AI chips grapples with fallout from reports of two extramarital affairs involving its longtime leader. Report by Jack Pownall and Eliza Herbert.

item.title: Russia's 'hidden mobilization': The 'expendable' lives fueling Putin's war on Ukraine
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome John Lough, Senior Research Fellow and Head of Foreign Policy & International Partnerships at the New Eurasian Strategies Centre (NEST Centre), He is also an Associate Fellow with the Russia & Eurasia Programme at Chatham House. Lough offers a sobering assessment of the social and strategic dynamics sustaining Russia's invasion of Ukraine. He argues that the Kremlin has disproportionately recruited soldiers from poorer and politically marginalised communities, including ethnic minority regions, where the human cost of the conflict is less likely to generate organised opposition. Many of those recruited, he explains, "have been recruited for a deliberate reason because they were seen, you know, ultimately as lives that were expendable, in other words as cannon fodder."

item.title: Suspect in Trappes racist attack says he acted 'on behalf of France'
item.description: In police custody, Kévin Tessier, the main suspect of the October 23 racist terror attack in Trappes, said he was acting "on behalf of France" when he went on a deadly rampage that killed one and left five injured. Investigators also found a sticky note at his home where he had listed names and phone numbers of left-wing figures.

item.title: Nvidia board weighs ouster of CEO Jensen Huang amid spy scandal
item.description: Nvidia's board met late Wednesday to consider removing chief executive Jensen Huang, after reports of two extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy, fuelled a market sell-off and raised questions about the AI chipmaker's leadership.

item.title: CCTV images released of night bus driver was shot dead in London
item.description: Police believe a bus driver who was shot dead in south London was not the intended target - and was in the wrong place at the wrong time.

item.title: Paraguay partially refunds Ueno Bank depositors after collapse
item.description: Paraguay's Central Bank said Wednesday it had partially returned savings to all eligible Ueno Bank depositors, following the lender's collapse last week. The crisis triggered mass protests and the impeachment and arrest of former president Santiago Peña, who is accused of directing government funds to the bank.

item.title: World's fastest ocean liner is sunk to break another record: largest artificial reef
item.description: The SS United States broke trans-Atlantic speed records. On Wednesday, it was sunk off the Florida coast and will become a diving destination and home for marine life.

item.title: Nvidia board reportedly preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after alleged affairs
item.description: The Nvidia board is reportedly planning to oust CEO Jensen Huang amid reports he engaged in two extramarital affairs.

item.title: Fiery clashes erupt in Spain as millions join general strike
item.description: Unrest broke out in cities across Spain on Wednesday after millions of workers joined the country's first general strike in 14 years.

item.title: Live: Ukraine faces 'systematic' restrictions to Starshield satellite network, Zelensky says
item.description: Ukraine has faced “systematic” restrictions to Starshield, the military satellite network crucial to downing Russian drones, along the whole front line and in occupied areas in recent days, President Volodymyr Zelensky said. Ukraine's contract with the US-based SpaceX service for accessing the network expires next year. Follow our liveblog for live updates.

item.title: WATCH: ABC's Bob Woodruff's foundation honors wounded soldiers and their families
item.description: David Muir speaks with "The Resilient" – a band made up of wounded soldiers – backstage at Bob Woodruff's annual Stand Up for Heroes, raising millions for veterans and military families.

item.title: Sharp rise in deadly antibiotic-resistant infections
item.description: Hundreds of people are being diagnosed with potentially life-threatening antibiotic-resistant infections each week, new figures suggest.

item.title: Democrat Scott Colom wins historic Senate race in Mississippi
item.description: Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi after a final count on Wednesday, becoming the state's first Black US senator since Reconstruction. His narrow victory adds to the Democrats' midterm gains as President Donald Trump's party suffers a series of defeats.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV returns to second homeland Peru and a nationwide welcome
item.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Peru on Wednesday for the final leg of his South American tour, returning to the country where he spent more than two decades as a missionary and bishop. Thousands gathered to welcome him home as “Padre Robert”, with many hoping his visit will bring attention to the country's poverty, crime and political instability.

item.title: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate race
item.description: Democrat Scott Colom has won election to the U.S. Senate in Mississippi, according to a race call by the Associated Press, defeating Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.

item.title: European leaders gather in Dublin under the shadow of hybrid threats
item.description: Ireland is mounting the largest security operation in its history as around 50 European leaders gather in Dublin this week amid growing concerns over hybrid attacks. The operation follows a wave of hoax bomb threats targeting airlines and media organisations across Europe, with Irish police reporting new incidents on Monday and Tuesday. FRANCE 24's Olivia Bizot reports.

item.title: Gadi Eisenkot unveils agenda to reverse Netanyahu’s policies
item.description: The bloc of Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot introduced a series of bills at the start of the legislative session that target Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his policies. They include launching an official government-led inquiry into the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attacks, setting term limits on the position of prime minister and overturning changes the outgoing Netanyahu-led government made to limit the powers of the judiciary. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Rina Bassist, Editor at Al-Monitor.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to major prisoner swap as peace talks end
item.description: Kyiv and Moscow on Wednesday agreed to a large-scale prisoner exchange as the final day of peace talks in Abu Dhabi came to an end, though neither side gave a concrete figure. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will meet separately with Russian President Vladimir Putin and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky on Thursday.

item.title: Several Democrats missed the crucial Hegseth impeachment vote. Many blamed traffic
item.description: Eleven Dems missed the critical vote, squandering Hegseth's impeachment attempt.

item.title: DR Congo's Tshisekedi paves way for constitutional change
item.description: In tonight's edition: A new law expanding the conditions for a constitutional referendum has ignited political tensions in DR Congo. Also, Kenya has officially declared the end of its latest Ebola outbreak. And at the COP31 climate summit, environmental advocates are warning against waste incineration, arguing that it risks locking African cities into expensive and polluting infrastructure.

item.title: Discharge petition on 2nd Epstein files bill secures 218 signatures
item.description: A discharge petition to force a vote on the Epstein Files Transparency Act II has amassed 218 signatures, teeing up additional floor action on the prospective bill.

item.title: General strike over housing brings out hundreds of thousands in Spain
item.description: Millions of workers in Spain shut down businesses and public transport on Wednesday, as part of the country's first general strike in 14 years. Following a peaceful march in Barcelona over soaring rents and property prices, and the rising cost of living, protesters smashed storefronts, set off small bonfires, burned bins and launched fireworks towards police. The unrest comes just weeks before snap elections, called by Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid.

item.title: Rare Marilyn Monroe photos from her final shoot to be auctioned
item.description: Prints from the personal collection of renowned photographer Bert Stern, including his celebrated series The Last Sitting of Marilyn Monroe, are set to be auctioned at Gros & Delettrez in Paris, marking the first such sale of Stern's private archives. At the heart of the Dec. 2 auction is The Last Sitting, a series of photographs taken in June and July 1962 at the Hotel Bel-Air in Los Angeles, just weeks before Monroe's death. FRANCE 24's Olivia Bizot reports.

item.title: France turns back Israeli settler representative upon arrival in Paris
item.description: French authorities forced Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan to leave the country after he landed at a Paris airport last week, his office said in a statement on Wednesday. The French foreign ministry did not confirm his deportation, only saying that Dagan was banned from French territory due to his involvement in Israel's illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank.

item.title: RSF calls for release of French reporter Christophe Gleizes, detained in Algeria
item.description: After being detained for almost 500 days in Algeria, Christophe Gleizes is no closer to being freed. Those close to him, as well as his fellow sports journalists have campaigned tirelessly for his release with the affair even attracting the attention of Zinedine Zidane, manager of the French football team. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Thibault Bruttin, Director General of Reporters Without Borders. He says that Gleizes has probably become "a token in a diplomatic game that we don't totally understand, that we don't totally master, up to the point where we are asking ourselves 'has he become a state hostage?'".

item.title: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent moved to a military base: Sources
item.description: Bessent is the latest administration official to move to a military base.

item.title: Biden says he wouldn't have run for a second term in 2024 if he knew he had cancer
item.description: Joe Biden says he didn't know he had cancer while he was president and wouldn't have sought a second term if he'd already been diagnosed

item.title: Why is gasoline suddenly under $4 a gallon?
item.description: The average price of a gallon of gasoline dipped below $4 this week for the first time in months. Does that mean more relief is coming for drivers?

item.title: General strike over housing brings out tens of thousands in Spain
item.description: Tens of thousands of protesters marched across Spain on Wednesday during a general strike over housing affordability and purchasing power just weeks before an early general election. Unions reported a significant response in some sectors in Spain's first nationwide 24-hour stoppage since 2012, but business leaders played down the participation. Braving heavy rain, tens of thousands of demonstrators marched through central Madrid carrying placards shaped like houses and chanting "We have no home" as they called for more affordable housing. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid.

item.title: Undone by a honey trap? Nvidia's Jensen Huang at heart of China spy scandal
item.description: It turns out that the new masters of the universe are human – all too human. Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang has admitted to an extramarital affair with Singapore-based Chinese tech CEO Alice Huang, who is no relation. She's under scrutiny over the purchase of Nvidia state-of-the-art chips that may have been smuggled back to the mainland illegally.

item.title: Tens of thousands attend Polish nationalist march days after shootings
item.description: Tens of thousands of Polish nationalist sympathisers gathered in Warsaw Wednesday for an annual Independence Day March, just days after a deadly shooting spree in Krakow that shook the country. The event is held each November 11 to commemorate the ending in 1918 of 123 years of partition by Russia, Prussia and Austria. The event is a magnet for all shades of Poland's right wing -- from conservative-nationalists aligned with its Law and Justice (PiS) party to far-right and radical groups. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland reports.

item.title: Schools evacuated across Italy after bomb threats
item.description: Schools were evacuated across Italy on Wednesday following a series of hoax bomb threats, but Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said there was no "concrete danger". Similar hoax threats were reported in schools in Britain and Ireland, which reportedly prompted some evacuations in Scotland. Meloni said she had called a government meeting with security and intelligence chiefs for Wednesday to discuss the threats. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

item.description: President Donald Trump spoke at a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery honoring fallen soldiers and addressed the war with Iran.

item.description: Pope Leo closed an emotional visit to Argentina with an appeal for unity and reconciliation, offering a message of hope to his predecessor's polarised homeland.

item.title: Greetings from Senegal, where breakdancers are competing in the Youth Olympics
item.description: Senegal's breakdancers have been practicing for their country's historic hosting of the Youth Olympic Games this month. It's the first time Africa is hosting an Olympic event.

item.description: A deportation flight carrying Iranians was abruptly turned around shortly after takeoff Tuesday, according to sources, marking the second such flight to be aborted.

item.description: Nine members of the Kennedy family have joined the legal fight against Trump's D.C. arch, arguing it would disrupt views and cast shadows over their ancestors' graves at Arlington National Cemetery.

item.description: For the swing voters NPR is regularly checking in with as part of its Swing Shift series, the election results brought mixed emotions, as does the pending Democratic control of Congress.

item.description: Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a large exchange of prisoners of war. U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi led to this decision, marking the biggest humanitarian release since the war began in 2022.

item.description: Four grizzly bears captured in Canada were responsible for killing a mother and daughter earlier this month, officials have said.

item.description: Sophie has visited the Rohingya refugee camps at Cox's Bazar in Bangladesh to see the support being offered to displaced people from Myanmar.

item.description: The tax was introduced in response to steep cuts to California's healthcare funding that resulted from the passage of President Donald Trump's "Big Beautiful Bill."

item.description: At least 12 people have been killed in two motorway pile-ups in eastern Bulgaria, the country's health minister said.
